short_title: Use income groups as a starting lens, not a verdict
recommendation: Report emissions and decoupling by income group, and always show how many countries in each group depart from the group pattern.
next_step: Add a line to every group chart that states the share of countries that do not follow the group pattern (for example {dec_notdec_pct_high}% of high-income countries did not decouple).
success_measure: Every group chart in the next report carries counts per group and a departure share.
caveat: Groups are defined from income, so group results partly restate the income result. The current World Bank classification is applied to all years.

short_title: Track decoupling over several years and with two kinds of emissions
recommendation: Measure decoupling over rolling multi-year windows, and report production-based and consumption-based CO2 side by side.
next_step: Add consumption-based CO2 for the {w1_consumption_countries} countries that have it, and report both decoupling shares for the same countries and years.
success_measure: Both shares are published together, with the gap between them quantified.
caveat: Consumption-based data cover far fewer countries. This project did not test how much of the measured decoupling is imported emissions.

short_title: Do not use the Week 3 model for yes/no decisions
recommendation: Use the model only as a ranking aid, for example to decide which countries to look at first, and always show its precision next to the base rate.
evidence_claims: test_prauc_lr; test_prauc_persistence; test_mcc_lr; test_rec_lr; top_prec_lr; ph_lr_minus_group
next_step: Never publish yes/no flags at the frozen threshold (it called {test_fp_lr} windows decoupling that did not decouple, and cleared only {test_tn_lr}). If a shortlist is needed, take the top-scored fifth and report its precision with an interval.
success_measure: No country is labelled as one that will decouple on the model's say-so. Any shortlist reports precision against the base rate.
caveat: The ranking gain is modest, comes largely from the income gradient (post hoc), and rests on one test period.

short_title: Test the forest and boosting models on later data before trusting them
recommendation: Freeze the random forest and gradient boosting settings as they are and score them once on windows that begin after the test years, as soon as later income data allow.
next_step: Write the comparison plan first, then score the later windows once and compare with persistence and the income-group base rate.
success_measure: A pre-specified comparison with paired intervals that either confirms or removes the advantage seen after the fact.
caveat: The earlier advantage was seen after the test set was opened. Windows ending in 2020 to 2022 were shaped by the pandemic.

short_title: Treat the slope-difference finding as provisional
recommendation: Do not build further claims on the idea that the income-emissions slope is flatter at high income until it is replicated.
next_step: Describe it as suggestive. Repeat the same pre-specified test on a later cross-section, or on a panel with country effects.
success_measure: Replication with the original plan and without exclusions, or a clear decision to drop the claim.
caveat: Income groups are defined from income, so a slope that differs by group is partly circular.

short_title: Pin data versions, hash raw files and refresh once a year
recommendation: Record the version of every raw file, store checksums that survive line-ending changes, and refresh once a year with a change report.
next_step: Re-run the lineage check on every refresh, keep income classifications by year, and hash files in a way that does not depend on Windows or Linux line endings.
success_measure: Every refresh produces a list of changed values, and checksum tests pass on a fresh clone on both systems.
caveat: Pinning records a version; it does not stop the World Bank or OWID from revising values later.

short_title: Show uncertainty beside every headline and write the plan before the results
recommendation: Print an interval or count next to every headline number, and commit the analysis plan before looking at results.
audience: Everyone who writes or reads reports
next_step: Use one format for headlines: number, interval, confidence badge. Keep the plan commit earlier than the results commit.
success_measure: Every headline in the next report has an interval or count and a badge, and the plan appears first in the history.
caveat: Intervals describe sampling noise. They do not cover wrong definitions or missing data.

short_title: Study structural drivers such as industry share and fuel mix more carefully
recommendation: Run a proper, pre-specified study of industry share, fuel mix and urbanisation, using a panel of country-years with country effects.
next_step: Add OWID's energy-mix shares, keep urbanisation separate, and test with the same robustness checks used in Week 2.
success_measure: Effect sizes with intervals that hold with PPP income and without small countries.
caveat: The results show association, not cause. Industry share also reflects goods made for export.
